T01_design_spike.title: Spike macOS mechanisms and write the Computer Use design
T01_design_spike.instruction:
Goal: ground the Computer Use design in evidence on this Mac, then write it down so every later node builds the same thing.

Steps:
1. Read docs/DESIGN.md (Browser M2, bridge, stores, packaging/signing sections), src/main/bridge.ts, src/main/browser/agent.ts, resources/browser-extension.ts, src/main/session-host.ts, electron-builder.yml and the Codex reference docs named in the context.
2. Write throwaway Swift spikes under /tmp (not in the repo) and run them with `swift` / `swiftc` to answer, with evidence:
   a. Can CGEventPostToPid deliver a left click and key events to a background (not frontmost, partially occluded) TextEdit window without moving the user's cursor? Which apps ignore it?
   b. Does AXUIElementPerformAction(kAXPressAction) / setting kAXValueAttribute work on a background app?
   c. Does SCScreenshotManager.captureImage(contentFilter: SCContentFilter(desktopIndependentWindow:)) capture an occluded window, and what scale/origin does the image have vs AX frames (points vs pixels on Retina)?
   d. TCC attribution: when Electron main spawns a helper binary directly vs launches an app bundle with `open -g -a`, which app does System Settings list for Accessibility / Screen Recording? With ad-hoc signing, does a grant survive rebuilding the helper (cdhash change)? Record the consequence: the helper must only be reinstalled when its own version changes.
3. Write docs/COMPUTER_USE.md (design spec, later folded into DESIGN.md by the docs node) covering: process model (helper app, install location ~/.pi-gna/computer-use/, versioned reinstall, LaunchServices launch, Unix socket path under the app's userData with a per-launch token); the JSON-RPC protocol (method names, params, results, error codes, notifications such as `cancelled`); AX tree text format with element indexes, how indexes are cached per app and invalidated, and the diff format; screenshot format (JPEG, max width, window-relative logical coordinates); input strategy (AX action first, CGEventPostToPid fallback, when to activate the window); settle-wait rules; overlay (virtual cursor + "pi is using <App> · Esc to cancel" pill); the computer_* tool list with parameter schemas mirroring Codex's; policy (enable flag, per-session allow-once, persisted always-allow, hard denylist bundle ids: Terminal, iTerm2, Ghostty, WezTerm, kitty, Alacritty, Warp, pi-gna itself and its helper, SecurityAgent/coreauthd/UserNotificationCenter-style security prompts), approval UX owned by main, one session per app at a time, cleanup on run end and Esc; settings page contents; risks and non-goals (no Windows/Linux, no locked-screen use, no JS REPL batching in v1).
4. Record spike results (what worked, what failed, exact API calls) in the doc's Evidence section.

Deliverables: docs/COMPUTER_USE.md. No product code.
Acceptance: every open question in step 2 has an observed answer or an explicit, labeled hypothesis; later nodes can implement from the doc without re-deciding the architecture. If evidence contradicts a plan-wide decision in the context, say so prominently in the doc and in your report.

T01_design_spike.report:
## Outcome
Wrote `docs/COMPUTER_USE.md`: the full Computer Use design (process model, JSON-RPC protocol, AX tree text
format, screenshot format, input strategy, settle-wait rules, overlay, `computer_*` tool list, policy, settings
page, risks/non-goals), grounded in Swift spikes run directly on this Mac (macOS 26.4.1, Apple M2) against
TextEdit/Calculator. No product code changed.

## Facts Learned
- **(a) `CGEventPostToPid` works on a fully backgrounded, fully occluded window.** Posted key events and a
  click+release to TextEdit while Finder (then Calculator, moved to TextEdit's exact window frame, 100% covering
  it on screen) was frontmost; text landed in TextEdit's `AXTextArea` (read back via AX, e.g. `"abc"`, `"tdf"`),
  AX focus moved to the text area after the click, `NSEvent.mouseLocation` never changed, and
  `frontmostApplication` never changed. `SCWindow.isOnScreen` stayed `true` even when 100% covered — that flag
  means "not minimized", not "not covered"; do not use it to detect occlusion.
- **(b) `AXUIElementSetAttributeValue(kAXValueAttribute)` and `AXUIElementPerformAction(kAXPressAction)` both work
  on a backgrounded app**, confirmed by read-back, `kAXErrorSuccess` (0), and the frontmost app never changing.
- **(c) `SCScreenshotManager.captureImage(contentFilter: SCContentFilter(desktopIndependentWindow:))` captures an
  occluded window correctly, but only if `SCStreamConfiguration.width/height` are set explicitly** — the default
  (unset) configuration returned an unrelated 1920×1080 image for a 586×488-point window; setting
  `width/height = frame * NSScreen.main!.backingScaleFactor` (2.0 here) gave the correct 1172×976 image, matching
  the window exactly, occluded or not. `SCWindow.frame` and the matching AX element's
  `kAXPositionAttribute`/`kAXSizeAttribute` frame are both points, top-left origin, and were numerically identical
  in every test — no AX↔ScreenCaptureKit coordinate conversion is needed, only a point→pixel scale for the capture
  call itself. `SCShareableContent` also lists off-screen phantom windows for a pid (a hidden `Untitled` window
  alongside the real `"Untitled 2"`); filter to `isOnScreen == true` and prefer the one whose frame matches AX's.
  A bare CLI process must call `_ = NSApplication.shared` before using ScreenCaptureKit or it aborts
  (`CGS_REQUIRE_INIT`); irrelevant for the shipped helper (a real `.app`) but relevant for any future test harness.
- **(d) TCC attribution and ad-hoc signing survival — NOT directly observed** (would require granting real
  Accessibility/Screen Recording permission and mutating this dev machine's TCC database, an irreversible,
  shared-system change not appropriate for a throwaway spike). Documented in COMPUTER_USE.md as an explicit,
  labeled hypothesis, grounded in: Apple's documented "responsible process" TCC model (favors a LaunchServices-
  launched app bundle over a directly spawned binary for clean attribution — matches Codex's helper existing as a
  separate `.app` outside `ChatGPT.app`), and this repo's own **already-verified** fact in `docs/DESIGN.md`
  (Updates section) that an ad-hoc signature's designated requirement is the build's `cdhash`, confirmed again
  here directly on Codex's installed helper (`codesign -dv`: `CDHash=f3f22a62...`, `TeamIdentifier=2DC432GLL2` —
  Codex has a real Developer ID team, which is *why* its grants survive updates and pi-gna's ad-hoc helper will
  not have that same luxury). Consequence recorded prominently in the doc: the helper must only be reinstalled
  into `~/.pi-gna/computer-use/` when its own embedded version changes, never on every pi-gna launch/update, or a
  pi-gna update would silently revoke the user's grant. Flagged in the doc's Risks as needing a real
  grant/rebuild/re-check before shipping.
- The `@oai/sky`/`@oai/cua` doc paths named in the task packet
  (`.../docs/skills/oai_sky_lib/macos/SKILL.md`, `sky-window2-api.md`, `tinysky-alt-core-cua-repl.md`,
  `tinysky-alt-confirmations.md`) **do not exist** on this machine. Only the installed
  `~/.codex/computer-use/Codex Computer Use.app` (bundle id `com.openai.sky.CUAService`, `LSUIElement`, built with
  AX/ScreenCaptureKit/overlay windows, includes a `CUALockScreenGuardian.app` — evidence it treats the locked-screen
  case as a real risk) and its per-app `AppInstructions/*.md` (Slack/Notion/Spotify usage notes, not an API
  reference) are present. The protocol/tool-shape sections of the doc are built from the task packet's own prose
  description of Codex's tool surface, not from reading those missing files; this gap is called out explicitly in
  the doc (preamble and the final Risks bullet) rather than silently papered over.

## Decisions Made
- Helper app `pi-gna Computer Use.app`, built under `native/computer-use/`, shipped inside the pi-gna bundle,
  installed to `~/.pi-gna/computer-use/` with a version-gated reinstall (compare `CFBundleVersion`), launched via
  LaunchServices (`-g`, no activation) rather than a direct child-process spawn, so TCC attributes grants to the
  helper's own bundle id and a grant is not invalidated by every pi-gna rebuild (only by a Computer Use version
  bump) — directly following from evidence (d).
- JSON-RPC 2.0 over a Unix socket under `userData/computer-use/<pid>.sock` with a per-launch token, following the
  bridge's existing token-gates-identity pattern (`src/main/bridge.ts`).
- AX action first, `CGEventPostToPid` fallback, window raise only as a last-resort, narrowly-scoped fallback when
  an app is empirically found to ignore backgrounded input — never as the default, since (a) and (b) show
  background delivery works for the apps tested.
- Policy enforced in main at the bridge route itself (not only in the extension), per the plan-wide decision that
  the bash tool can call the bridge directly; hard denylist is a fixed list (terminals, pi-gna + helper bundle
  ids, security-prompt processes), separate from the revocable "always allow" store.
- No JS REPL/batching in v1 (the one source doc that might have justified it, `tinysky-alt-core-cua-repl.md`, is
  unavailable here); discrete `computer_*` tools only, one JSON-RPC call per tool call.

## Files Touched
- `docs/COMPUTER_USE.md` (new) — the full design document described above.

## Interfaces Changed
None (design document only; no code, no protocol implementation yet).

## Verification
- Doc-only change; no `pnpm typecheck`/`pnpm test`/`pnpm build` are affected by this node (confirmed `git status`
  shows the commit touched only `docs/COMPUTER_USE.md`; the working tree's other modified/untracked files are
  pre-existing, unrelated ATP infrastructure work and were left untouched).
- All claims in the Evidence section are backed by actual Swift spikes run and observed in this session (scripts
  were under `/tmp/cu-spike`, removed after use per the node's "not in the repo" instruction); exact output is
  quoted/paraphrased in the doc's Evidence section (e.g. `"abc"`, `"tdf"` AX read-backs; `1172 x 976` vs the wrong
  default `1920 x 1080`; `CDHash=f3f22a62...` from `codesign -dv` on the installed Codex helper).

## Risks
- Evidence (d) is a labeled hypothesis, not observed; the implementation node that first ships the helper should
  verify the ad-hoc-cdhash/TCC-grant interaction for real (grant Accessibility, rebuild the helper, confirm the
  grant is lost) before relying on the version-gated-reinstall design as the whole mitigation.
- Evidence (a)'s "which apps ignore postToPid" is answered only for two native AppKit apps (TextEdit, Calculator);
  Electron/Chromium-hosted target apps and any DRM'd/game-style app were not tested and may need the
  activate-and-restore fallback more often than native apps do.
- The Codex API reference docs named in the task packet do not exist on this machine; the protocol/tool-shape
  design is derived from the packet's own description of Codex's tool surface, not verified against Codex's own
  docs. If those docs exist elsewhere (a different machine, a different Codex version), re-check the protocol
  section against them before building the helper.

## Recommended Next Step
Claim the next node (implementing `native/computer-use/` and/or the bridge route) with `docs/COMPUTER_USE.md` as
its primary reference; it should start by verifying evidence (d) for real (grant, rebuild, re-check) before
finalizing the install/reinstall logic, and should test input delivery against at least one Electron/Chromium
target app to confirm or refute the (a) hypothesis about such apps needing activation.

T02_helper_scaffold.title: Scaffold the Swift helper app, build script and JSON-RPC socket server
T02_helper_scaffold.instruction:
Goal: a buildable native helper "pi-gna Computer Use.app" that main can launch and talk to, with permission checks, and nothing else yet.

Steps:
1. Follow docs/COMPUTER_USE.md (from T01). Create native/computer-use/ (Swift Package or plain sources compiled by swiftc; no third-party Swift deps). Target macOS 14+.
2. Implement an LSUIElement app (no Dock icon) whose entry point reads launch arguments (socket path, token, parent pid), listens on the Unix domain socket, accepts one client that must present the token first, and serves newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0. Exit when the parent pid dies or the socket closes for good.
3. Methods: `ping` (version, pid), `permissions` (AXIsProcessTrusted, CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess), `request_permissions` (AXIsProcessTrustedWithOptions prompt, CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess), `open_settings` (accessibility | screen_recording System Settings panes). Structured errors per the design's error codes. Leave a dispatch table that later nodes extend.
4. Add scripts/build-computer-use.mjs and a `build:computer-use` package.json script: compile a universal (arm64 + x86_64) binary, assemble the bundle (Info.plist with bundle id, version from package.json or a helper version constant, LSUIElement, usage strings, icon optional), ad-hoc sign it, output to build/computer-use/ (gitignored). Print the output path.
5. Add a tiny manual smoke script (scripts/computer-use-smoke.mjs) that launches the built app with `open -g -a`, connects, sends ping and permissions, and prints the replies.

Deliverables: native/computer-use/ sources, build script, smoke script, .gitignore entry.
Acceptance: `pnpm build:computer-use` succeeds; the smoke script prints a ping reply and the current permission status; the app shows no Dock icon and exits when the smoke script exits; pnpm typecheck passes.

T02_helper_scaffold.report:
## Outcome
Buildable `pi-gna Computer Use.app` (Swift, LSUIElement, universal arm64+x86_64, macOS 14+, ad-hoc signed) with a token-gated JSON-RPC 2.0 Unix-socket server. `pnpm build:computer-use` outputs `build/computer-use/pi-gna Computer Use.app`. Smoke script launched it via `open -g -a`, got hello/ping/permissions replies, and the helper exited (socket removed) when the client closed.

## Facts Learned
- `open -g -a <app> --args --socket .. --token .. --parent ..` passes args fine; no `-n` needed for the smoke run.
- Helper (launched via LaunchServices) reports accessibility=false, screenRecording=false on this Mac (not granted yet).
- Plain `swiftc` per-arch + `lipo` is enough; no SwiftPM needed.
- build/ already holds the tracked icon.icns, so only `build/computer-use/` is gitignored.

## Decisions Made
- Plain sources compiled by swiftc (native/computer-use/Sources/*.swift); the build script reads `helperVersion` from Protocol.swift and writes it as CFBundleVersion and PigCUHelperVersion; CFBundleShortVersionString = package.json version.
- Methods: hello (token auth, first message), ping, permissions {prompt?}, request_permissions, open_settings {pane: accessibility|screen_recording}, shutdown. Error codes -32001..-32010 enum defined; unauthorized/parse/method-not-found use standard-ish codes (-32600/-32700/-32601).
- Dispatch table: global `methods` dict; later nodes add handlers from their own file and call a register function from `registerMethods()` in Protocol.swift. Handlers are synchronous.
- Exit conditions: authenticated client disconnect, `shutdown`, parent pid dead (1 s timer), SIGTERM/SIGINT, accept failure.

## Files Touched
native/computer-use/Sources/{main,Protocol,Permissions,Server}.swift, scripts/build-computer-use.mjs, scripts/computer-use-smoke.mjs, package.json (build:computer-use), .gitignore.

## Interfaces Changed
New helper CLI args `--socket --token --parent`; JSON-RPC methods above; `pnpm build:computer-use`.

## Verification
- `pnpm build:computer-use` OK; `node scripts/computer-use-smoke.mjs` printed hello, ping, permissions replies and "helper exited: true"; pgrep showed no leftover helper.
- `pnpm typecheck` passes. (pnpm test/build not affected; not run.)
- Dock icon absence rests on LSUIElement=1 in Info.plist, not visually checked.

## Risks
- Handlers run on the socket thread, not main; later AppKit/overlay work must hop to main. Single client at a time; a second connection waits.
- Unauthenticated connection closes the connection but keeps the helper alive (only an authenticated disconnect exits it), so the parent-pid watch is the backstop.
- TCC/ad-hoc cdhash behavior (design evidence d) still unverified.
- Electron packaging (extraResources) not wired yet.

## Recommended Next Step
Install/launch/client in main (src/main/computer/), then helper methods list_apps/get_state on this dispatch table.

T03_helper_apps_ax.title: Implement app inventory and the indexed accessibility tree in the helper
T03_helper_apps_ax.instruction:
Goal: the helper can list apps, resolve and background-launch one, and return its accessibility tree as compact indexed text with diffs.

Steps:
1. Follow docs/COMPUTER_USE.md. Add methods `list_apps` (running apps via NSWorkspace plus installed apps in /Applications, /System/Applications and ~/Applications; id = bundle id, displayName, isRunning, windows [{id, title}]) and `resolve_app` (display name, bundle id or path -> bundle id, pid; launch in the background with NSWorkspace.openApplication(activates: false) when not running, wait for its first window).
2. Add `get_app_state` {app, window_id?, disable_diff?, include_screenshot? (wired in T04)}: walk the AX tree of the target window (and its open menus/sheets/popovers), depth- and size-limited, skipping invisible and zero-size elements; emit one line per useful element in the design's format, e.g. `[42] AXButton "Sign in" (Press, ShowMenu)`, `[7] AXTextField "Search" value="foo" focused`, with indentation for hierarchy; include focused element, selected text and window title in a header.
3. Keep an element cache per app: index -> AXUIElement plus frame, reset on every full read. Diff mode returns added/removed/changed lines vs the previous text for that app; the first read and disable_diff return the full tree. Element indexes stay valid only until the next state read (document this in the method's error text).
4. Refuse denylisted bundle ids here too (defense in depth) with the design's error code.
5. Extend the smoke script: `list_apps`, then `get_app_state` for TextEdit (launch it in the background) printed in full and as a diff after typing into it manually.

Deliverables: helper sources, smoke script update.
Acceptance: TextEdit and Calculator return readable indexed trees under the design's size cap; launching does not steal focus; a second read shows a diff; denylisted apps are refused; the build script still produces a universal signed app.

T05_helper_input.title: Implement background input actions in the helper
T05_helper_input.instruction:
Goal: the helper performs Codex-equivalent UI actions on background apps without moving the user's cursor or stealing focus where macOS allows it.

Steps:
1. Follow docs/COMPUTER_USE.md input strategy and the T01 spike evidence.
2. Methods (all take {app, ...}; element_index refers to the latest get_app_state cache, stale index -> clear error asking for a fresh state):
   - click {element_index | x,y, mouse_button?, click_count?}: element -> AXPress (or AXConfirm/AXPick where appropriate), falling back to a synthesized click at the element's center; coordinates are window-relative logical points from the last screenshot mapping; synthesize with CGEventPostToPid (mouse down/up, click state for double clicks, right/middle buttons) without warping the cursor.
   - drag {from_x, from_y, to_x, to_y}; scroll {element_index | x,y, direction, pages?} (AX scroll actions when exposed, else scroll-wheel events posted to the pid).
   - press_key {key}: xdotool-style names and chords (Return, Tab, Escape, BackSpace, Up/Down/Left/Right, Page_Up, Home, F1-F12, KP_0, super/cmd/ctrl/alt/shift+key, Control_L aliases) mapped to virtual keycodes and flags.
   - type_text {text}: unicode keyboard events to the focused element of the app.
   - set_value {element_index, value} (kAXValueAttribute); select_text {element_index, text, prefix?, suffix?, selection_type text|cursor_before|cursor_after} (kAXSelectedTextRangeAttribute); perform_secondary_action {element_index, action} (only actions the element exposes; list them in the error otherwise).
   - paste {text, format text|md|html}: save the general pasteboard, write the content (html as public.html with a plain-text fallback, md as plain text), send cmd+v to the app, restore the previous pasteboard.
3. When an action provably needs the window frontmost (per spike evidence, e.g. apps ignoring pid-targeted events), activate it as a documented fallback and report that in the result.
4. Settle wait: after an action, the next state read waits ~1 s, extended up to 5 s while AXBusy or a progress indicator is present (AXObserver notifications or polling).
5. Extend the smoke script with a scripted TextEdit run: type, select a word, replace it via set_value, press cmd+a, read state; and a Calculator run clicking digits by element index.

Deliverables: helper sources, smoke script update.
Acceptance: the scripted runs succeed with TextEdit and Calculator behind another window, the user's cursor never moves, and the clipboard is restored after paste; every failure path returns a structured error.

Handlers must run concurrently per app: a per-app serial queue, including its settle waits, must never block calls for other apps, so two chats can drive two apps at once. Verify against T04b's fixture app while the user's frontmost app stays frontmost; this replaces the TextEdit/Calculator scripted runs in step 5.

T06_helper_overlay.title: Add the virtual cursor overlay and Esc-to-cancel to the helper
T06_helper_overlay.instruction:
Goal: the user always sees what pi is doing and can stop it, like Codex's agent cursor and "using your computer · Esc to cancel" pill.

Steps:
1. Follow docs/COMPUTER_USE.md overlay section.
2. Create a borderless, transparent, click-through NSWindow per display at a level above normal windows (ignoresMouseEvents, joins all spaces, excluded from ScreenCaptureKit captures so screenshots never contain it). Draw an agent cursor (pi-gna accent colors) that animates to each action point over the target window, with a short click ripple; draw a small pill near the target window: "pi is using <App> · Esc to cancel".
3. Methods: `overlay_show {app, session_label}`, `overlay_hide`; input actions from T05 move the cursor automatically when the overlay is shown.
4. While the overlay is shown, a global key monitor (NSEvent global monitor; requires Accessibility) catches Esc and sends a JSON-RPC notification `cancelled {app}` to the client, then hides the overlay. Optionally detect strong user input on the target window and report it the same way if the design asks for it.
5. Respect reduced motion. Hide the overlay when the client disconnects.

Deliverables: helper sources, smoke script update showing the overlay during the TextEdit run and printing the cancelled notification when Esc is pressed.
Acceptance: the cursor and pill appear over the target window during actions, never appear in screenshots, Esc produces exactly one cancelled notification, and the overlay disappears on disconnect.

UPDATE (orchestrator): Codex orders its cursor relative to the target window (VirtualCursor.move(to:aboveWindowID:relativeToWindow:...) in its helper), not as a full-screen top-level overlay. Do the same: order the cursor window just above the target window's number, so whatever covers the target also covers the cursor and nothing ever sits over the user's work. One cursor and pill per app being driven (apps run in parallel). The overlay never becomes key and never activates pi-gna or the helper. The user types in other apps while pi works, so a global Esc must not cancel a run they did not mean to cancel: decide from evidence when Esc counts (e.g. only while the target window, the pill or pi-gna is frontmost or under the pointer) and document it.

T09_bridge_route_policy.title: Add the /computer bridge route with main-enforced approvals, app locks and cleanup
T09_bridge_route_policy.instruction:
Goal: the single gate between pi sessions and the helper: every computer_* call is authorized, serialized and cleaned up by main.

Steps:
1. Follow docs/COMPUTER_USE.md. Create src/main/computer/agent.ts with a computerRoute(...) registered on the AgentBridge as POST /computer in src/main/index.ts, like browserRoute in src/main/browser/agent.ts.
2. Per-session queue (pi runs one message's tool calls in parallel) and a per-app lock: one session operates an app at a time; a second session gets a clear "busy, used by another chat" error.
3. Authorization in main: refuse when Computer Use is disabled or the app is denylisted; an app neither always-allowed nor allowed for this session triggers an approval the user answers in the window (Allow once / Always allow / Deny), never something the token holder can answer, since bash inherits PIGNA_TOKEN. Implement it by reusing the existing approval card: SessionHost injects a select-style extension UI request with a main-owned id into that session's renderer stream and resolves the response in main instead of forwarding it to pi (read src/main/session-host.ts and the renderer's extension UI handling first; if that cannot be done cleanly, add a minimal dedicated IPC approval request rendered by the same card component). Always allow writes the store; Allow once lasts until the session's process ends.
4. Map actions to helper calls; show the overlay on a session's first action on an app (session label = chat name) and hide it and release the app lock when that session's run ends (SessionHost agent_end / process exit) or after an idle timeout.
5. The helper's `cancelled` notification aborts that session's run through the same path as the Stop button, releases the lock, and makes the pending tool call fail with "Stopped by the user (Esc)".
6. Unit tests with a fake service: denylist, disabled, approval allow-once/always/deny, lock contention, cleanup on run end, Esc cancel.

Deliverables: src/main/computer/agent.ts, SessionHost/index.ts wiring, tests.
Acceptance: pnpm test and pnpm typecheck pass; no path lets a bridge caller act on an app the user has not approved.

UPDATE (orchestrator): the per-app lock serializes only the same app; different apps from different chats must run in parallel end to end (route queue, service calls, helper). Cover two sessions driving two apps concurrently in the tests.

T04b_codex_background_input.title: Find and prove how Codex drives background apps without stealing focus
T04b_codex_background_input.instruction:
Goal: find out how the Codex app's Computer Use clicks, types and scrolls in background apps without activating them, stealing keyboard focus or moving the user's cursor, prove an equivalent in a Swift spike, and amend docs/COMPUTER_USE.md so T05 implements it. The user must be able to keep working in other apps while pi uses one.

Why: T01 found that CGEventPostToPid / SLEventPostToPid clicks (with window-number fields, a mouseMoved first, and SLPSPostEventRecordTo) were ignored by TextEdit, so the design fell back to activating the app and warping the cursor. That fallback is unacceptable: it takes over the user's desktop.

Leads from the orchestrator's static look (nm/strings only) at ~/.codex/computer-use/Codex Computer Use.app/Contents/MacOS/SkyComputerUseService:
- Classes: SyntheticAppFocusEnforcer, SystemFocusStealPreventer, KeyWindowTracker, SystemFrontmostApplicationTracker, VirtualCursor. Fields: activationEventTap, activationEventSuppression, FocusStealSuppression, lastViewBridgeFocusStealWasSuppressed, realActivationObserved / frontmostAppActivated / targetDeactivated / lastEventTime, SetFrontProcessOptions, targetPID, targetWindowID, cursorWindowID, correspondingWindowID.
- APIs: NSEvent mouseEventWithType:location:modifierFlags:timestamp:windowNumber:context:eventNumber:clickCount:pressure: and otherEventWithType:...windowNumber:...; windowNumberAtPoint:belowWindowWithWindowNumber:; GetProcessForPID (ProcessSerialNumber); dlopen/dlsym with /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ paths (private SkyLight symbols resolved at runtime; their names are not plain strings); _CGSMainConnectionID; CGSSessionScreenIsLocked; kCGSSessionSecureInputPID; AXEnhancedUserInterface / AXManualAccessibility (to enable AX in Chromium/Electron apps); CGShieldingWindowLevel; VirtualCursor.move(to:aboveWindowID:relativeToWindow:...); no CGEventPost/CGEventPostToPid import (posting is likely through dlsym'd SkyLight calls).
- Hypothesis (unverified): Codex makes the target process believe it is active and its window key (synthetic focus via SkyLight process and event-record calls, like yabai's focus-without-raise using _SLPSSetFrontProcessWithOptions and SLPSPostEventRecordTo), sends window-targeted events carrying the window number, and suppresses or immediately reverts any real activation the target triggers (event tap plus frontmost tracking), so the system's frontmost app, the user's key window and the cursor never change.

Steps:
1. Static analysis of the Codex binaries only (SkyComputerUseService, SkyComputerUseClient, the Package_*.bundle contents): nm, strings, otool -ov (ObjC metadata), `swift demangle`, `otool -tV` disassembly around the classes above, to find which private symbols are resolved with dlsym (look for how the names are built or obfuscated), the call order for one click and one key press, and how focus-steal prevention works. Do not attach a debugger to, inject into or drive running Codex processes, and do not copy OpenAI code: record API names and call sequences only.
2. Prior art with web_search/fetch_content: yabai (focus without raise: SLPSPostEventRecordTo byte records, _SLPSSetFrontProcessWithOptions with kCPSUserGenerated / kCPSNoWindows), Hammerspoon, alt-tab-macos, and public write-ups on background clicks to AppKit windows (CGEventSetIntegerValueField with kCGMouseEventWindowUnderMousePointer / ...ThatCanHandleThisEvent, kCGEventTargetUnixProcessID, NSEvent windowNumber posted to a pid).
3. Build a fixture AppKit app under /tmp (text field, text view, buttons, checkbox, scroll view, a menu with key equivalents, a context menu) that logs each event it receives plus NSApp.isActive and whether its window is key. Launch it hidden. While another app stays frontmost, prove that left, double and right click, drag, scroll wheel, typing and cmd-shortcuts (cmd+a, cmd+v) reach it. Repeat read-only or fixture-scoped checks against one SwiftUI and one Chromium/Electron window you launched yourself.
4. Around every action, assert the user's frontmost app, key window and NSEvent.mouseLocation are unchanged, and that the fixture never shows up in front.
5. Amend docs/COMPUTER_USE.md: replace the "activate + warp the cursor" rung with the proven mechanism (exact calls and order, which private symbols, macOS version caveats, how activation attempts by the target are suppressed or reverted), list what still cannot be done in the background and say those actions must fail with a clear error (never silently activate), and state that the helper must run actions for different apps concurrently (per-app queues; T02's handlers currently run synchronously on the socket thread).

Deliverables: docs/COMPUTER_USE.md amendments with spike evidence; spike sources stay in /tmp (summarize them in the doc). No product code.
Acceptance: a reproduced sequence that clicks and types into a background AppKit window with the user's frontmost app, key window and cursor unchanged. If that proves impossible, fail this node with evidence of exactly what Codex does differently and the options, so the user decides; do not fall back to focus-stealing.

## Outcome
Reproduced a mechanism that clicks (left/double/right), drags, scrolls, types and runs menu actions in a background AppKit window, a SwiftUI window and an Electron window while the user's frontmost app, key window and cursor stay unchanged. docs/COMPUTER_USE.md amended (callout, new "Input strategy" rungs 2/3, "Cannot be done in the background", "Concurrency", Evidence e). The activate+warp fallback is removed.

## Facts Learned
- Codex (static read only): SynthesizedEvent builds NSEvent mouse events with a window number -> CGEvent, sets fields, calls WindowServerSPI.setWindowLocation(CGEvent, point); notifyAppActivated/Deactivated/KeyFocus are NSEvent AppKit-defined events; SyntheticAppFocusEnforcer tracks "believes active" vs truly active. Matches yabai/cua-driver.
- Required: NSEvent.mouseEvent(windowNumber: wid).cgEvent (field 51 = window) + SkyLight SLEventSetWindowLocation(ev, window-relative top-left point) + postToPid. Without the window location nothing hit (32 variants). Scroll/key need only field 51 = wid.
- yabai activate record (SLPSPostEventRecordTo: b[4]=0xf8,b[8]=0x0d,b[0x8a]=1,wid@0x3c) makes the app believe it is active without changing the front process; make_key records (b[8]=1,2; b[0x3a]=0x10; 0xff fill) make the window key without raising. Needed for text selection/focus in text views. Deactivate with b[0x8a]=2 afterwards.
- Target window must be ON SCREEN: hidden apps (open -j), minimized, other Spaces drop clicks. My earlier misses were caused by `open -j`.
- A mouse down in a non-topmost window makes AppKit raise it to the top of the stack (frontmost app/key window unchanged). Fix: AXRaise the user's AXFocusedWindow afterwards; works. SLSOrderWindow from another process fails (error 1000).
- Menu key equivalents (cmd+a/v/1) do not fire in the background even with synthetic focus; AXPress on the matching AXMenuItem works.
- Electron: left/double/right/scroll/typing all trusted and landed; no primer click needed. SwiftUI fine.
- Context-menu item click via posted mouse events to the menu window not proven (use AXShowMenu + AXPress).
- Sources: https://cua.ai/blog/inside-macos-window-internals (trycua/cua), https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/2609, yabai src/window_manager.c (focus_window_without_raise, make_key_window).

No foreground fallback of any kind; failures are explicit errors. Per-app serial queues in T05 (different apps concurrent). z-order restored with AXRaise only if front app unchanged.

docs/COMPUTER_USE.md (commit). Spike sources in /tmp/pigna-fixture/spike-src (not in repo).

None in code. Doc spec changes: rung 2 recipe, no rung 3, helper handlers must dispatch per-bundleId queues.

## Verification
Fixture drivers /tmp/pigna-fixture/drv2 (AppKit: 11+ checks all PASS with front/keywin/cursor unchanged, z restored), drv4 on SwiftUI and Electron (UNCHANGED reported; Electron's CHANGED line was only my AXRaise restoring pi-gna above its launch position). Frontmost app (pi-gna) and mouse (837,392) identical before/after the whole session. Only fixture pids terminated; temp Electron userdata dir removed. No pnpm checks run (docs only).

Private SkyLight SPI and record layout can break on a macOS update. TextEdit/Calculator not retested (etiquette). Brief z-order flicker (~100 ms) on pointer clicks. Canvas/game apps unsupported. Chromium user-activation-gated actions untested.

T05: implement the recipe in Swift (dlsym wrappers, synthFocus, per-app queues, AXRaise restore, menu-key AX lookup), fail explicitly for unsupported cases, and verify against TextEdit once installed.

## Outcome
Live verification done through the route path below the UI (see Decisions). All step-2 checks pass or have an evidenced gap. One real defect found and fixed (screenshot of the wrong window). Grants intact at the end. Two items need the user: a macOS screen-capture prompt that is open right now, and Esc plus visual review.

## Facts Learned
- **Open macOS prompt (user action):** on the first screenshot macOS 26 shows a modal "pi-gna Computer Use is requesting to bypass the system private window picker and directly access your screen and audio" with Allow / Open System Settings (UserNotificationCenter, log: tccd AUTHREQ_ATTRIBUTION). It appeared even though Screen Recording is granted, and it is why NSWorkspace.frontmostApplication read com.apple.UserNotificationCenter for the whole run (constant, not caused by an action). I did not click it. Screenshots worked while it was pending. The user should click Allow once; macOS may re-ask periodically.
- **Defect, fixed:** the route took the screenshot with `screenshot {app}`, so the helper picked the app's largest window while the AX tree came from the focused window. With several TextEdit documents the tree said "Untitled 4" and the picture showed another document (a full-screen one), and click x,y mapping would have followed the wrong window. Fix is TS only (agent passes `window_id: state.windowId`; protocol type gets optional window_id); no helper change, no reinstall needed.
- Without a window_id, a minimized window makes the helper fall back to the app's next window (here the user's "Untitled 3"), so a get_app_state is read-only safe but a write would land in that other document. Expected behaviour (the main window is chosen like Codex), noted as risk.
- Helper-level proof for minimized window: click with window_id of the minimized window returned the background-unsupported error ("window is not on screen (minimized...); background input cannot reach it") with the desktop unchanged. The route cannot pass window_id, so through the route this case only appears when ALL windows are off screen.
- Overlay windows (cursor 96x96, pill 228x28) are layer 0 windows ordered directly above their target window and below the user's covering pi-gna window; both are removed on release (window list before/after).
- Approval card returns again for a chat after `release` (end of run) by design; Always allow persists (computer-use.json), Deny is remembered per chat and Calculator was not launched after Deny.
- Unreproduced: once, TextEdit asked the same chat for approval again mid-session; a rerun of the same sequence (3 times, notification logging on) did not repeat it.
